summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, status post failed kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and recent ischemic colitis, was admitted for progressively worsening watery diarrhea and diffuse abdominal pain lasting three days. He denied fever, vomiting, or rectal bleeding. CT abdomen/pelvis showed mild colonic wall thickening, most consistent with mild colitis, possibly acute on chronic, but not typical for ischemia. Stool studies were negative for C. difficile, Salmonella, and Campylobacter. His symptoms resolved within 12 hours of admission, and he was diagnosed with likely viral gastroenteritis. He underwent scheduled hemodialysis without complications. Amlodipine was discontinued due to hypotension during dialysis. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with gastroenterology for possible colonoscopy and to obtain a repeat chest CT in six months for a new 7 mm left upper lobe nodule.
